lesson.child_mission: Nets are 2D arrangements of faces that fold into a 3D object without overlapping faces in space.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which is a valid cube net idea: a straight row of 6 squares, or a cross of 6 squares? Explain briefly.

FEEDBACK
Cross can work; a single straight row of 6 does not fold to a closed cube.

WATCH FOR
Drawing overlapping faces in a net makes it impossible to cut from one sheet cleanly.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Draw six nets (cubes and pyramids/prisms). Mark one invalid net and explain why it fails.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Draw six nets (cubes and pyramids/prisms). Mark one invalid net and explain why it fails. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Cross can work; a single straight row of 6 does not fold to a closed cube. Reasoning: I used net by attending to fold rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Drawing overlapping faces in a net makes it impossible to cut from one sheet cleanly. Correction: Cross can work; a single straight row of 6 does not fold to a closed cube. Why: the correction restores accurate use of net.

Parent: Likely misconception: Drawing overlapping faces in a net makes it impossible to cut from one sheet cleanly. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses net with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with net, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

teach_steps.explain:
Nets are 2D arrangements of faces that fold into a 3D object without overlapping faces in space.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
